# Closest-result comparison

| Source | Object | Hypotheses | Conclusion | Difference from Paper 01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Menotti–Onofri (1981) | Heat-kernel plaquette action on SU(N) | Finite lattice gauge action | Defines and analyzes the action | Does not study a frustrated one-link conditional LDP or Dobrushin coefficients. |
| Varadhan (1967) | Heat kernel on a manifold/diffusion | Elliptic diffusion; small time | Logarithmic squared-distance asymptotic | Supplies an imported leaf; no lattice incidence or conditional product. |
| Dobrushin (1968) | Gibbs specifications | Conditional kernels close to independent | Sufficient regularity/uniqueness criteria | Paper 01 tests and violates the row hypothesis for one gauge specification; it does not challenge the theorem. |
| Liggett–Schonmann–Stacey (1997) | Dependent binary random fields | Strong conditional lower bounds / finite dependence structures | Product domination | Paper 01 invalidates one proposed route to the required conditional rarity; it does not disprove domination by other routes. |
| 't Hooft (1979) | Global electric/magnetic flux sectors | Periodic/twisted boundaries | Flux duality and free-energy relations | Global and topological; Paper 01 is local, open-block, and conditional. |
| Mack–Petkova (1980) | Vortex condensation and confinement condition | Boundary-vorticity free energies | Sufficient confinement mechanism | Retains the cost of vorticity; Paper 01 diagnoses what is lost by a worst-boundary supremum. |
| de Forcrand–von Smekal (2002) | SU(2) 't Hooft loops and flux free energies | Finite-temperature lattices | Numerical flux-sector/confinement evidence | Different observable, scale, and proof type. |
| Balaban (1987–1989) | Gauge-field RG effective densities | Small/large-field decompositions | Localized effective actions and ultraviolet stability statements | Does not assume uniform flatness under arbitrary microscopic conditioning; not displaced by the obstruction. |

## Stabilized novelty boundary

The defensible contribution is theorem-level synthesis, not novelty of ingredients: the paper proves that an explicitly realizable local central boundary forces metric-barycenter concentration and thereby defeats a boundary-uniform rare-defect quantifier and the associated microscopic Dobrushin row criterion. It also proves open stability and a compact-group extension that do not rely on unique geodesics.

The manuscript does not claim priority for central frustration, heat-kernel LDPs, Dobrushin theory, twisted boundaries, or constructive RG.
